The second release candidate for Lucid 0.1.0, a web client for your CalDAV calendars and tasks that you run yourself. Since the first one, repeating events and tasks keep their days and times across time zones and daylight saving time, and the month view steps by scrolling.

Lucid 0.1 is for early adopters: it reads and writes your real calendars, so try it with a test calendar first. [Status and limits](https://github.com/tbckr/lucid#status-and-limits) lists what is missing, such as reminders and invitations.

## New

- In the month view, scrolling steps one month, down to the next and up to the previous. A month taller than its window scrolls first, and a trackpad's momentum never skips a month.

## Fixed

- A repeating event or task from another time zone, such as a meeting on Tuesdays at 18:00 in New York seen in Berlin, shows its repeat on the days it falls on in yours, in the details and in the editor. Changing its repeat no longer moves it to other days or an hour off, nor brings back events you deleted. [Time zones](https://github.com/tbckr/lucid#time-zones) explains how Lucid reads such a series.
- A changed repeat saved for all events from a later event, such as "Every month on day 10" from the event of 10 November, repeats on the day the editor names, not on the day the series started.
- An event of a series moved to another day no longer gives the repeat that day: in rc.1, changing the repeat of a series on Tuesdays from its event moved to a Monday could move the whole series to Mondays.
- Times that a change to or from summer time skips or repeats, such as 02:30 on the night Berlin changes to summer time, are read as the iCalendar standard (RFC 5545) says. A series another app saved at such a time no longer shows an hour off every day, and a series at 02:30 keeps its time when you move, split or change it from its event that night, or check off a task's repeat there.
- Moving an event of a series, by drag or in the editor, offers "All events" only where Lucid can save it. rc.1 could offer it and then refuse the move, or leave it out where it works, for a series stored in UTC and for an event moved on its own.
- Lucid uses zod 4.6.7, which fixes a memory exhaustion while validating very large lists ([GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5)). zod runs only in the browser, so at worst calendar data could crash a tab, not the server.

## Upgrading from rc.1

No setting changed. Lucid keeps nothing of its own, so a series that rc.1 saved on the wrong days or an hour off stays that way on your server: if you changed the repeat of a series from another time zone, from an event moved to another day, or for all events from a later event, check it and correct it in the editor.

## Known issues

- A series that starts at a time summer time skips, such as 02:30 on the night of the change in Europe or the US, repeats an hour off on every other day: at 01:30 when entered in the editor, at 03:30 when created from the calendar ([#10](https://github.com/tbckr/lucid/issues/10)).
- A changed repeat saved for all events can leave the series' first event off the repeat: a weekly series that started on a Tuesday, changed to Fridays from a later event, keeps its first Tuesday ([#11](https://github.com/tbckr/lucid/issues/11)).

Not yet tried on a real machine: the double-click start on Windows and macOS, Safari, the Home Manager service on Ubuntu and the launchd agent on macOS.

## What to test

- Scrolling through the month view with a mouse wheel and with a trackpad, also in a low window.
- Repeating events and tasks from another time zone, such as a calendar someone abroad shares with you.
- CalDAV servers other than Nextcloud: if yours doesn't work, the problem report (account menu, **Report a problem**) tells us why.

Please tell us how it went in [Discussions](https://github.com/tbckr/lucid/discussions).

## Install

- **On your own computer:** download the archive for your system below, extract it and double-click `lucid`.
- **On a server:** the container image `ghcr.io/tbckr/lucid:0.1.0-rc.2`, the deb, rpm or Arch package below, or the NixOS module from `github:tbckr/lucid/v0.1.0-rc.2`. A release candidate moves neither `latest` nor `stable`.

The [README](https://github.com/tbckr/lucid#quick-start) explains each.
